statement: At a party every woman dances with at least one man, and no man dances with every woman. Show that there exist men $M$, $M'$ and women $W$, $W'$ such that $M$ dances with $W$ and $M'$ dances with $W'$, but $M$ does not dance with $W'$ and $M'$ does not dance with $W$.

$P$ is a point inside triangle $ABC$. The line through $P$ parallel to $AB$ meets $AC$ at $A_0$ and $BC$ at $B_0$; the line through $P$ parallel to $CA$ meets $AB$ at $A_1$ and $BC$ at $C_1$; the line through $P$ parallel to $BC$ meets $AB$ at $B_2$ and $AC$ at $C_2$. Find the point $P$ such that $A_0B_0 = A_1C_1 = B_2C_2$.

Given $k > 0$, the sequence $(a_n)$ is defined by its first two terms and $a_{n+2} = a_{n+1} + \dfrac{k}{n}a_n$.

a) For which $k$ can $a_n$ be written as a polynomial in $n$?

b) For which $k$ can $\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}$ be written as $\dfrac{p(n)}{q(n)}$ for polynomials $p, q \in \mathbb{R}[X]$?
Show that there exists $n > 2$ such that $1991 \mid \underbrace{19\!\underbrace{99\cdots9}_{n}1}_{\text{(with } n \text{ nines)}}$.

Let $P_0 = (1,0)$, $P_1 = (1,1)$, $P_2 = (0,1)$, $P_3 = (0,0)$, and for $n \geq 0$ let $P_{n+4}$ be the midpoint of $P_n P_{n+1}$. Let $Q_n$ be the quadrilateral $P_n P_{n+1} P_{n+2} P_{n+3}$ and $A_n$ its interior. Find $\bigcap_{n \geq 0} A_n$.
